deviations: cJSON_GetErrorPtr: A failed parse returns the error's offset; the bridge keeps the input and that offset (cJSON.c's global_error) for cJSON_GetErrorPtr.

cJSON_InitHooks: cJSON's allocator hooks are C function pointers: the bridge keeps them (cJSON.c's global_hooks) and allocates C items and strings with them; Rust code allocates through its c_json::Store.
cJSON_malloc: Allocates with cJSON's C allocator hooks, which the bridge keeps; Rust code allocates through its c_json::Store.
cJSON_free: Frees with cJSON's C allocator hooks, which the bridge keeps; Rust code frees through its c_json::Store.

ctest:cJSON_test: cJSON_test is one program whose exit status is its result: main prints the version and checks print_preallocated on six items; each of those is a Rust test. The C only compared the preallocated print with cJSON_Print's text when it failed; the Rust tests always compare them.
ctest:cjson_add: One Rust test per RUN_TEST of the Unity program. Its failing_hooks (cJSON_InitHooks with a malloc that fails) are a Store over an Arena whose allocations fail while set.
ctest:compare_tests: One Rust test per RUN_TEST of the Unity program; its zeroed cJSON items on the stack are new Arena items.

ctest:json_patch_tests: One Rust test per RUN_TEST, over the same files of tests/json-patch-tests. cjson_utils_rs's JSON Patch runs over cjson_rs's Arena through a Json adapter in the test, whose object lookup walks the members as cJSON_GetObjectItem does.
ctest:minify_tests: One Rust test per RUN_TEST of the Unity program, minifying the same bytes as C strings (their NUL included). The last one also checks what the minify leaves.

ctest:misc_tests: One Rust test per RUN_TEST. Without a Rust meaning, and so not translated: the null pointers the Rust API's slices can't be (cJSON_Parse, cJSON_ParseWithOpts and cJSON_Minify of NULL, cJSON_CreateIntArray and the other array constructors of NULL, cJSON_PrintPreallocated into a NULL buffer), cJSON_InitHooks(NULL), and reading an item cJSON_Delete freed (deallocated_pointers_should_be_set_to_null instead checks that delete frees the item and its string; the Arena refuses freed items). cJSON_SetBoolValue, a macro of cJSON.h, is a helper of the test; failing_realloc is a PrintStorage whose reallocation fails; the deep parse runs on a thread with a large stack, as the C's main thread has.

ctest:misc_utils_tests: cjson_utils_rs's functions run over cjson_rs's Arena through a Json adapter in the test. The Rust test also checks the statuses of the patches it applies, and that no item is left.

ctest:old_utils_tests: One Rust test per RUN_TEST, with cjson_utils_rs's functions over cjson_rs's Arena through a Json adapter in the test. sort_tests also checks that it compared all 25 neighbours, and the merge tests that no item is left.

ctest:parse_array: One Rust test per RUN_TEST, parsing the same C strings (their NUL included) with c_json::parse_array on a ParseBuffer; the static item is an Arena item, and common.h's reset and assertions are helpers of the test.
ctest:parse_examples: One Rust test per RUN_TEST, over the same files of tests/inputs. Where the C compared cJSON_GetErrorPtr with the input, the Rust tests check the error offset parse returns.
ctest:parse_hex4: One Rust test per RUN_TEST, with c_json::parse_hex4 on the same digits.
ctest:parse_number: One Rust test per RUN_TEST, with c_json::parse_number on the same C strings. The C compared the numbers within Unity's double precision; the Rust tests compare them exactly.

ctest:parse_object: One Rust test per RUN_TEST, parsing the same C strings with c_json::parse_object on a ParseBuffer; the static item is an Arena item, and common.h's reset and assertions are helpers of the test.

ctest:parse_string: One Rust test per RUN_TEST, parsing the same C strings with c_json::parse_string on a ParseBuffer and comparing the decoded bytes (the UTF-8 of the C's euro sign, cat and cat face spelled as bytes).
ctest:parse_value: One Rust test per RUN_TEST, with c_json::parse_value on the same C strings.

ctest:parse_with_opts: One Rust test per RUN_TEST. parse_with_opts returns the parse end, or the error offset that cJSON_GetErrorPtr and return_parse_end point to; a NULL input or error pointer has no Rust meaning, so parse_with_opts_should_handle_null checks the calls with real inputs.
ctest:print_array: One Rust test per RUN_TEST, with c_json::parse_array and c_json::print_array into 1024 bytes that may not grow, as the C test's printbuffers.

ctest:print_number: One Rust test per RUN_TEST, with c_json::print_number into the 26 bytes the C prints into. The C's rewrite of three-digit exponents (for MinGW and old MSVC printf) isn't needed: the Rust prints two digits on every platform. print_number_should_print_non_number, ignored in C89, checks that NaN and the infinities print as null.
ctest:print_object: One Rust test per RUN_TEST, with c_json::parse_object and c_json::print_object into 1024 bytes that may not grow, as the C test's printbuffers.
ctest:print_string: One Rust test per RUN_TEST, with c_json::print_string_ptr into 1024 bytes that may not grow; the C's NULL string is None.
ctest:print_value: One Rust test per RUN_TEST, with c_json::parse_value and c_json::print_value into 1024 bytes that may not grow, as the C test's printbuffer.
ctest:readme_examples: One Rust test per RUN_TEST: the README's examples on the crate's safe API with an Arena, also checking that deleting the monitor frees every item.
source_left: fuzzing/** (23 files, which project.exclude keeps out of the port)
library_config/** (5 files, which project.exclude keeps out of the port)
tests/unity/** (127 files, which project.exclude keeps out of the port)

The port is finished: all 25 units were committed, and the final clean build passed with 165 Rust tests. The run (`20261116-231855-1d6d`) took about 7 hours and exited with code 0. Everything is on the branch `codecoremorph/20261116-231855-1d6d`, from `acc76239bee0` to `fa128fe65fc2`. Your working tree and `main` are unchanged, and nothing has been merged.

## Units

| Units | What | Attempts | Commit |
|---|---|---|---|
| U-0001 | `cJSON.c` → `rust/cjson_rs` | 3 | `40ecc17b04ad` |
| U-0002 | `cJSON_Utils.c` → `rust/cjson_utils_rs` | 1 | `3eaa4c503b2a` |
| U-0003 – U-0024 | The 22 C test files → `rust/cjson_rs/tests/*.rs` | 1 each, except U-0020 (2) | `70804e243d69` … `2cfa6482bc0f` |
| U-0025 | Deleting the C, the CMake build, the bridges and the C tests (automatic, 40 files) | 0 | `fa128fe65fc2` |

The three retries:
- **U-0001, attempt 1:** a test file I wrote kept a `#pragma warning(disable` line copied from `cJSON.c`, and a safety rule rejects any new warning suppression.
- **U-0001, attempt 2:** the check that exported functions match the C signatures only looks at files changed in that attempt, so it reported every function as missing. Attempt 3 passed.
- **U-0020, attempt 1:** clippy rejected a hand-written value of π, so I replaced it with `std::f64::consts::PI`.

## Coverage and parity
- **Rule coverage:** all 92 sites of the module rule, all 22 test files and all 27 deletions.
- **Before:** the original build had 22 C tests, all passing, with none failing, flaky or skipped.
- **After:** the final build ran 165 Rust tests and all passed. Every C function is mapped to Rust (92 entries), every C test is paired with Rust tests (22), and the final code has no `unsafe`.

## What wasn't verified
- **Output comparison:** CodeCoreMorph didn't run its check that compares the program's output before and after, because that needs a Make build.
- **`tests/unity_setup.c`:** it is only compiled under MSVC, so it was never built.
- **Shared libraries:** the shared-library and `BUILD_SHARED_AND_STATIC_LIBS` configurations weren't tested.
- **Root `Makefile`:** it still names `cJSON.c` and will need updating or removing.
- **Out of scope:** `fuzzing/`, `library_config/` and `tests/unity/` were excluded by the manifest and left alone.

## Behavior that differs from the C
- **Number formatting:** printing numbers was reimplemented and ignores the locale's decimal point.
- **Allocation failure:** if memory runs out while a string is being parsed, the reported error position can differ.
- **NaN:** the integer value (`valueint`) of a NaN number is `INT_MIN`.
- **Null strings:** a null string no longer crashes.
- **`cJSON_Utils` quirks:** these were kept on purpose.
- **Allocator hooks:** `cJSON_InitHooks`, `cJSON_malloc` and `cJSON_free` existed only for the C side and were deleted with it.
- **Tests:** C tests that pass NULL weren't translated, because the Rust API can't take a null. A test that read a freed item now checks the deletion instead.

## Follow-up worth doing
`cjson_utils_rs` works through a `Json` trait. Once the C side was deleted, the only implementations of that trait left are adapters inside `cjson_rs`'s tests. Before anyone uses the utils crate outside the tests, a real implementation for `cjson_rs`'s document type should go into one of the crates.

## How to review
```
git log acc76239bee0..codecoremorph/20261116-231855-1d6d
git diff acc76239bee0 codecoremorph/20261116-231855-1d6d
```
The full report is at `E:\codecoremorph-trials\c-eval\cjson\.codecoremorph\runs\20261116-231855-1d6d\report.md`. I've left the merge to you.

I can turn this summary into a page you can share if it's going to others.
